mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT at t-0w signals a broad activity shock that will suppress discretionary shopping trips for the next four weeks, keeping RETAIL_REC below its prior four-week mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above the previous 28-day mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not recover within four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL exceeds 20 points above baseline, households substitute away from out-of-home shopping, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next one to two weeks even if other mobility series are flat.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL crosses above 20 points above baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within two weeks after RESIDENTIAL first exceeds 20 points above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous worsening in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS indicates a broad reduction in local outing intensity; when both fall together, retail-and-recreation mobility also weakens over the next four weeks because the same trip-making channel is being compressed.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline after weeks in which both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS are below their prior week values.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week from an already depressed level, the move reflects an abrupt access shock that quickly feeds through to shopping trips and pushes RETAIL_REC lower within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week from a level below -40
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week after TRANSIT drops more than 5 points from below -40.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises while WORKPLACES falls, the implied stay-at-home substitution reduces discretionary errands and lowers RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks; the effect is strongest when both moves occur together.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not underperform its prior four-week average after periods where RESIDENTIAL increases and WORKPLACES decreases in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in PARKS over two consecutive weeks indicates colder or less favorable outing conditions, which typically lowers casual shopping traffic with a lag of two weeks and keeps RETAIL_REC below trend.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decrease within two weeks after PARKS falls for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, recovering TRANSIT together with rising WORKPLACES restores access to shopping districts and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks; the signal fails if mobility rebounds but retail does not.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week mean despite simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: The combined late-drop in GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES at t-0w marks a broad reduction in out-of-home routines; that shock should carry through to lower retail-and-recreation mobility over the next one to two weeks before any household adjustment dissipates.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within two weeks after both GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES drop sharply in the same week.
